subject: Ebb & Flow renewal: approval request for bespoke concession package
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Ebb & Flow renewal: immediate approval request

Team —

Quick summary: Ebb & Flow (Prod: patient-monitoring) is at EOY renewal; ARR: $720k. They flagged an RFP from a competitor and procurement is threatening to move unless we materially improve commercial terms. Account exec (me) has been on calls with Carlos (CFO) and Priya (Head of Ops) — primary asks below. Customer is sensitive to uptime history (they had one incident last fall) and wants stronger SLA + a short-term concession to commit to 24 months.

Customer asks (verbatim):
- 20% first-year discount on list (applied as upfront credit)
- Full SLA uptime credit pool: $150k (one-time credit) to cover perceived risk
- Term reset: allow 12 months remaining to be treated as new 24-month agreement with a 12-month price lock
- Longer data retention (audit logs) for 24 months (adds compliance cost)

What I recommend to save the deal (based on churn risk and strategic value):
- Approve a structured concession: 12% ACV discount year 1 (applied as invoice credit), $75k SLA credit (one-time), 24-month term with 12-month price protection, and commit to a Bi-weekly Ops review for first 6 months.

Why: 20% + $150k + extended retention is > our concession guardrails and exceeds the typical renewal playbook, but we can probably keep within ARR targets with a smaller package. If we say no, they will either go to the competitor or escalate procurement which will delay close by 6+ weeks and increase our churn risk.

Attachments: renewal-usage-report-June2026.pdf (customer usage + spike analysis), current-contract-EBB-2024.pdf.

Request: Executive sign-off on the recommended package or counter guidance by EOD Monday (2026-06-22) so we can get procurement redlines back before month-end.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
+1 415 555 0192

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ebb & Flow renewal: immediate approval request

Sean — thanks for the crisp brief. A few quick thoughts:

1) Pricing: 20% + $150k credit is outside of standard CFO approvals. I support a concession that is revenue-protective. The proposed 12% + $75k credit sounds reasonable as a starting point, but I want a structured cap and a clawback if usage drops 20% in 6 months.

2) SLA credit: we need clear trigger language and a cap tied to incidents — not an open cash reserve. Can legal/operations draft a schedule that limits credit to demonstrated SLA failures and ties credit release to root-cause remediation?

3) Data retention: adding 24-month audit logs increases storage and egress risk. We can offer as an add-on MSR with cost recovery. Recommend we include a one-time pass-through fee or a small monthly surcharge rather than absorbing.

4) Term reset: fine if we get a 12-month price protection and a minimum commit of 18 months net-new spend at their current run-rate.

Action: Monica, can you run a quick cost delta for 24-month retention and the incremental ops support? Jonas — we will need counsel on SLA language and the clawback. Sean — draft the proposed concession sheet (line-item credits, triggers, and timeline) and attach to the eSig packet.

Laura Bennett
VP, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ebb & Flow renewal: immediate approval request

Laura / Sean —

Attached is a quick delta: proposed 24-month audit-log retention will increase monthly storage cost by ~$3,200 (estimated), and we should add a $12k one-time ingestion/backup surcharge to cover snapshot work. Ops hours for Bi-weekly reviews estimated at 8 hours/month for first 3 months (approx $4k).

If the team wants to keep the net impact neutral, the simplest path is to pass the $12k onboarding + $3.2k/mo to the customer. If we want to be partially competitive, we could offer the first 3 months waived and then start charging.

Monica Patel
Sr. Manager, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-concession-sheet.xlsx

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-25T15:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ebb & Flow renewal: immediate approval request

Team — legal/finance notes:

- We will not approve an open-ended $150k SLA credit without factual incident accounting. If we go forward with a one-time credit it must be contingent on documented service degradation per our SLA (measured by incident timestamps and impact). Propose $75k as a conditional credit payable only after confirmed SLA breaches attributable to Redwood.

- Clawback: Affirmative. Include a 12-month clawback clause if gross ARR drops >20% within first 12 months after renewal. Clawback would convert unused credit into payable amounts.

- Term reset OK if we require a minimum 18-month committed spend or a non-cancelable clause for the first 12 months. No executive approvals for price resets beyond what Laura outlined.

I am prepared to sign off on: 12% year-one invoice credit, $75k conditional SLA credit (documented triggers), 24-month term with 12-month price protection, and 24-month audit-log retention with a $12k one-time pass-through and monthly surcharge of $3,200 (with first 3 months waived).

Jonas Weber
Head of Finance & Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Sharma <priya@ebbflow.health>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos@ebbflow.health>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ebb & Flow renewal: immediate approval request

Sean / Carlos —

Thanks for the rapid response and for the pragmatic counter. We discussed internally and the team is comfortable moving forward if Redwood will accept the package Jonas outlined: 12% invoice credit (applied Y1), $75k conditional SLA credit, 24-month term with first 12 months price protection, and Redwood covers the first 3 months of retention surcharge + $12k one-time onboarding fee.

Carlos will route the updated concession language through procurement next week and we should be ready to sign after legal cleans up the SLA triggers.

Can you send revised concession sheet and eSign link when ready?

Cheers,
Priya Sharma
Head of Operations
Ebb & Flow Health
